clue.text: Quite uncaring about the aged

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about, used before dates
the aged are old people, so this gives OLD

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of total indifference towards elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly indifferent is described as emotionally chilly, lacking all warmth.

clue.text: Looks up and down

indicators.note: the word reads the same whichever way you go, here the column read upwards or downwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone glances up and then down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' looks like part of the definition, but it tells you the answer reads the same in both directions in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at something is to observe it with the eyes.

clue.text: Virginia is a follower of Diana, a singer

indicators.note: a follower comes after, so the Virginia piece is placed after the Diana piece

parts.note: Di is the usual short form of the name Diana
VA is the postal abbreviation of the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A singer called Virginia is a devoted fan of someone named Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna, the leading female opera star, is a celebrated singer.

clue.text: The politician rates on in a frenzy

indicators.note: a frenzy is wild disorder, so the letters of the words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician gets worked up while ranting on about something.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an upper legislative chamber, such as the US upper house, is a politician.

clue.text: By no means a second-rate seaman!

definitions.text: By no means a second-rate seaman!

parts.words: By no means a second-rate seaman!
parts.note: split the answer into a prefix meaning inferior or second-rate plus a word for a sailor, then note that such an underwater sailor is no inferior one

explanation.surface: A tribute to a sailor who is anything but mediocre.
explanation.walkthrough: The prefix SUB- can mean below standard, and a MARINER is a seaman, so the word literally looks like 'second-rate seaman'; the clue denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew member serving aboard an underwater naval vessel is a kind of sailor.

clue.text: I have a left shoulder-blade that is a miracle of claimed Katisha

definitions.text: I have a left shoulder-blade that is a miracle of claimed Katisha

parts.words: I have a left shoulder-blade that is a miracle of claimed Katisha
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing last word of a boast sung by Katisha in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado

explanation.surface: A character in an operetta boasts of the beauty of her own shoulder-blade.
explanation.walkthrough: Katisha, the elderly lady in The Mikado, sings that her left shoulder-blade is a miracle of beauty; the solver supplies the final word of her line.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Katisha's line names physical beauty or attractiveness.

clue.text: Town boards shown around flat

indicators.note: the theatre word goes around the word for level, enclosing it

parts.note: the boards is a theatre term for the stage
flat means level or even

explanation.surface: A town puts up notice boards displayed around a block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: STEVENAGE is a town in Hertfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hertfordshire new town, built after the Second World War, is an English town.

clue.text: Business raised by a masterstroke

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
raised means up

explanation.surface: A business enterprise gets its funding raised through a clever move.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant, successful stroke or move is a sudden triumph of planning.

clue.text: Many tots need correction, it's argued

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: correction here means putting the preceding words right by rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Lots of small children require correcting, it is claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' reads as a verb in the surface but is fodder; 'correction' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disputed or challenged has been argued over.

clue.text: Newly-built parade it's quite incomparable

indicators.note: something newly built is constructed afresh, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A newly built parade of shops is said to be unlike anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Things so different in kind that they cannot be compared are fundamentally unlike.

clue.text: Top up the jar

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

explanation.surface: Someone refills the jar to the brim.
explanation.definitionFit: A cylindrical container for food or liquid is a kind of jar.

clue.text: Call Oriental person back

indicators.note: back tells you to read the combined pieces backwards

parts.note: E for East, the Orient
a person is a man

explanation.surface: Someone asks an Eastern person to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to designate or label them.

clue.text: A doctor some patients drive to despair

indicators.note: some of the following words' letters are taken, a run lying across two of them

explanation.surface: A doctor whose patients are driven to despair.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'driVE To'. The surface suggests a hopeless GP, but the doctor here treats animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal doctor is a veterinary surgeon, shortened in everyday speech.

clue.text: Disgusting homes-a lot must be changed

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are to be changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: A lot of homes need altering because they are revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive or detestable is disgusting.

clue.text: Sets aside for later-after the holidays

explanation.surface: Someone puts things aside for when the holidays are over.
explanation.walkthrough: Hold back: the second reading is LEAVES (holidays) plus OVER (after, finished) - the holidays are over.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something for later use is to keep it back; leave is time off work, and when it is finished it is done with.

clue.text: Women players receiving part payment

parts.note: read as performers in the theatre who are paid for taking a role, not sportswomen on partial wages

explanation.surface: Female sportswomen are being paid only some of their wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' and 'part payment' suggest sport and instalments; a part is a role in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Female performers on stage or screen are paid for the roles they play.

clue.text: The memorial constituents had seen to

indicators.note: the constituents, the component letters, of the following words are put together in another order

explanation.surface: Voters in a constituency arranged for a memorial to be put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like voters, but signals that the letters of HAD SEEN TO are the parts to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone set up over a grave is a memorial to the dead.

clue.text: Peer provided with hearing device by a trainee

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A nobleman is given a hearing aid by an apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: A British nobleman ranking above a viscount is a peer of the realm.

clue.text: Belligerent Roman poet

explanation.surface: A warlike Roman poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Warlike or military describes something belligerent; Marcus Valerius, author of epigrams, was a first-century Roman poet.

clue.text: Thrashing to make a scholar smart

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar
to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: A beating is meant to make a pupil hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe beating, or soundly defeating someone, is a thrashing in informal speech.

clue.text: Taking the B road with little hesitation — it's wider

parts.note: the words of the clue are simply taken as written, B and road
er is the little sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A driver hesitates before turning onto the minor road, which is more spacious.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a B road is a secondary road, below an A road.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of greater breadth is wider.

clue.text: Woman given note and present

parts.note: her refers to a woman
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A woman is handed a note and a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift; it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Present, as in attending, means being in this place.

clue.text: Getting more confident about the right tip to hand over

indicators.note: about means the confident word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: surer means more confident
R is the abbreviation for right
a tip is an end

explanation.surface: A man growing in confidence about the right tip decides to hand it over.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or relinquish something to another is to yield it.

clue.text: Born in a marine environment

indicators.note: in tells you the answer lies inside the run of the following words

explanation.surface: A creature born in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles 'mariNE Environment'. Nee, French for born, introduces a woman's maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for born is used before a married woman's original family name.

clue.text: Plant group

explanation.surface: A plant group.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant is to place firmly in position; a group is a collection of things that belong together.

clue.text: Works certain animals

explanation.surface: Someone tends to some animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Works means performs or carries out; female deer, rabbits and hares are called by this name.

clue.text: Coloured people standing up for William

parts.note: orange is a colour
men means people

explanation.surface: People of a certain colour support a man called William.
explanation.walkthrough: Orangemen are members of the Protestant Orange Order, named after William of Orange, King William III.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order champion the memory of King William III.

clue.text: Supports men

explanation.surface: Someone backs men.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropes holding a tent or mast firm are supports; fellows or blokes are men.

clue.text: Tea when the game's over?

explanation.surface: Teatime once the match has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American herbal infusion is a kind of tea; in chess the final winning move ends the game.

clue.text: Require 22 down before the first of December

indicators.note: before puts the cross-reference piece ahead of the letter taken

parts.note: the answer to 22 down, the word for born

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone wants a birth registered before the start of December.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require it.

clue.text: The French way appears inferior

parts.note: les is a French word for the, in the plural
S for south, a direction or way

explanation.surface: The French way of doing things appears to be worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Less, meaning lower in rank or importance, describes something inferior.

clue.text: Alternate always, or they become disorganised

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words become disorganised, thrown out of order

explanation.surface: People who switch constantly end up in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate, as in one of each pair, means skipping one each time.
